title: A program in modules
description:
This project has three files. `main.js` is finished: it reads lines like `add tea 250 2` and `total`, and uses two modules you write.

`money.js` exports:
- `parseCents(text)`: prices are typed in whole **cents**, so `"250"` returns the number `250`. Anything that is not a run of digits (`"2.50"`, `"abc"`, a missing price) throws an `Error` with the message `bad price`.
- `formatCents(cents)`: `250` becomes `"2.50"`, `5` becomes `"0.05"`.
- `CURRENCY`: the string `"EUR"`.

`cart.js` has a **default export**: a class `Cart` with `add(name, cents, qty)`, `remove(name)` (returns `true` if the item was there), and a getter `total` (sum of cents × qty). Adding a name again adds to its quantity, keeping the first price. It imports nothing from `main.js`.

starter.money.js: // Export parseCents, formatCents and CURRENCY from here.
starter.cart.js: // Export the Cart class as the default export.

hints: Named exports: `export function parseCents(text) { ... }`. The default export: `export default class Cart { ... }`, imported without braces.
A price is valid only when it is not missing or empty (`!text` catches both `undefined` and `""`) and every character is a digit: `[...text].every(ch => ch >= "0" && ch <= "9")`.

examples.name: a small order
examples.stdin:

add cake 425
total
done
examples.expected:

added cake
total 9.25 EUR

examples.name: same item twice and removing
examples.stdin:

add tea 300 1
total
remove tea
remove tea
total
done

added tea
total 7.50 EUR
removed tea
no tea
total 0.00 EUR
